title: Dvaita and beyond (Madhva, Ramanuja): the lover and the beloved stay two; why devotion needs difference (2 of 7)
hook: a teacher gives him a secret mantra; he climbs the temple tower and shouts it to the town
carry: two, and the space between is love
tomorrow: Dvaita and beyond (Madhva, Ramanuja): the lover and the beloved stay two; why devotion needs difference (3 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Dvaita and beyond, part one. Madhva, the Krishna in the ballast clay, and two, forever. Your line: two, and the space between is love. Did you enjoy someone's difference? Today, a third answer, from a teacher who came before Madhva. Day two hundred eighty-nine.

South India, around nine hundred years ago. A young scholar named Ramanuja walks, tradition says, eighteen times to the house of an old teacher, asking to be given a sacred mantra. Seventeen times he's turned away. The eighteenth time, the teacher gives it, with a warning: keep this secret. Tell no one, or you'll go to hell. Ramanuja walks straight to the temple, climbs the tall gateway tower, and calls the mantra out to everyone in the street below. The teacher is furious. Ramanuja says: if I go to hell and all these people are saved, I'll gladly go.
screen: `EIGHTEEN WALKS TO A TEACHER.` → `KEEP THIS SECRET.` → `SHOUTED FROM THE TEMPLE TOWER.`

segments.voice: The teacher, the story goes, embraced him. Ramanuja became the great teacher of the Sri Vaishnava tradition, centered at the temple of Srirangam, and he gave Vedanta a third answer. Not Shankara's not two. Not quite Madhva's two, which came about a century later. His school is called Vishishtadvaita: not two, but qualified. One reality, with real distinctions inside it. His picture is the body and the soul. You have a body, and you, the self, live in it, guide it, and are the reason it moves. The body is real. It's not a snake on a rope. But it isn't independent either. It's yours. For Ramanuja, the whole universe, every soul and every grain of matter, is the body of God. And God, Vishnu, Narayana, is the soul of it all. He found this in the Upanishads, in a passage where the sage Yajnavalkya describes the inner controller. Paraphrased: the one who dwells in the earth, yet is other than the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who guides the earth from within: that is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. So, for Ramanuja, you're really you, forever. God is really God. And yet God is closer to you than your own body is to you. That's why Ramanuja's tradition sees love and surrender to God as the path. The soul, freed, doesn't vanish into God. It enjoys God, as God's own. And the mantra from the tower? The tradition still teaches it openly.
screen: `VISHISHTADVAITA: QUALIFIED NOT-TWO.` · `THE WORLD IS GOD'S BODY.` · `THE INNER CONTROLLER.` · `REALLY YOU, REALLY GOD, VERY NEAR.` · then, large: `TWO, AND THE SPACE BETWEEN IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and feel your body from the inside. Your hands. Your chest rising. The weight of your legs. Notice that you're in it, living it, moving it, and it's really yours. Then try Ramanuja's picture, just as a picture: the room, the city, the trees, the people you love, all of it as one great body, with a life at its center that lives in you too. If you pray, you can rest in that nearness. If not, feel the body and the room, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Dvaita and beyond: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita. One reality, qualified. The world and souls are God's body, God is their inner self, and the soul stays itself, loving God.

Your line: two, and the space between is love. Today, share one good thing you've been keeping to yourself, a tip, a recipe, a kindness, the way Ramanuja shared the mantra. Day two hundred eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Sri Vaishnavas, followers of Ramanuja, worship Vishnu with Lakshmi, especially at temples like Srirangam, recite the Alvars' Tamil hymns alongside Sanskrit texts, and practice prapatti, surrender to God, as the heart of the path.

myth: Ramanuja kept the secret mantra as he was told
tradition says he shouted it from the temple tower so everyone could hear.
Ramanuja taught that the world is the body of God
God is the soul of all, and the world and souls are God's real body.
Ramanuja came first, around the eleventh and twelfth centuries; Madhva about a century later.

fork.setup: you're Ramanuja. after eighteen visits, your teacher gives you a mantra and warns: tell anyone, and you'll go to hell. what does tradition say you do?
options: shout it from the temple tower.
teach it only to your students.
fork.reveal: he climbs the tower and calls it out: if I go to hell and they're saved, so be it. his teacher, the story goes, embraced him.

original.note: Sanskrit: vishishta (qualified, distinguished) + advaita (not two): Ramanuja's school.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hindu philosophy has two options, one or two.
what it means: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita says one reality, God, with souls and world as God's real body.

what a scholar hears: Ramanuja (traditionally 1017–1137) grounds the body-soul relation (śarīra-śarīri-bhāva) in the Antaryami Brahmana, Brihadaranyaka 3.7; the 'secret mantra' in the tower story is usually identified as the eight-syllable Narayana mantra.

sources.ref: Ramanuja, Sri Bhashya and Vedartha Sangraha (the world as God's body)
Sri Vaishnava hagiography (Ramanuja and Tirukkoshtiyur Nambi; the temple tower)

notes: The tower story (Tirukkoshtiyur Nambi, eighteen visits, the eight-syllable mantra) is hagiography; confirm details.
Ramanuja's traditional dates (1017–1137) are given only as 'around nine hundred years ago'; many scholars place him somewhat later.
Outline groups Ramanuja under 'Dvaita and beyond'; the script is careful to call his school qualified non-dualism, not Dvaita.

Audit (2026-09-30, 10% sample): the review called Ramanuja 'the teacher who went beyond both' (ranks him above Shankara and Madhva, and he came before Madhva); now 'a third answer, from a teacher who came before Madhva'. The teach's conclusion is now attributed to Ramanuja rather than stated as fact.
